title: Impact of Very-Low-Birth-Weight Classification on Neonatal Mortality

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
This is a Regression Discontinuity Design (RDD) problem. The very-low-birth-weight classification creates a sharp cutoff at a specific birth weight threshold (likely 1500 grams), creating quasi-random assignment to treatment around this threshold. The key assumption is that there are no other factors that change discontinuously at the cutoff threshold - only the classification itself should jump at this point.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load required libraries
library(rdrobust)
library(rddensity)
library(ggplot2)

# Read the data
data <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s91_data.csv")

# Identify the cutoff point
cutoff <- min(data$running_var[data$treated == 1])
if(is.infinite(cutoff)) {
  cutoff <- max(data$running_var[data$treated == 0])
}

# Center running variable around cutoff
data$running_var_centered <- data$running_var - cutoff

# Main RDD analysis using rdrobust
rdd_result <- rdrobust(y = data$y, 
                      x = data$running_var_centered, 
                      c = 0,
                      p = 1,  # linear polynomials
                      kernel = "triangular")

# Print main result
cat("=== MAIN RDD RESULTS ===\n")
cat("Cutoff point:", cutoff, "\n")
cat("RDD Coefficient (Treatment Effect):", round(rdd_result$coef[1], 4), "\n")
cat("Standard Error:", round(rdd_result$se[1], 4), "\n")
cat("P-value:", round(rdd_result$pv[1], 4), "\n")
cat("95% CI: [", round(rdd_result$ci[1,1], 4), ",", round(rdd_result$ci[1,2], 4), "]\n")
cat("Bandwidth:", round(rdd_result$bws[1], 4), "\n")
cat("N left of cutoff:", rdd_result$N[1], "\n")
cat("N right of cutoff:", rdd_result$N[2], "\n")

# Robustness checks

# 1. Different bandwidths
cat("\n=== ROBUSTNESS: DIFFERENT BANDWIDTHS ===\n")
bw_half <- rdrobust(data$y, data$running_var_centered, h = rdd_result$bws[1]/2)
bw_double <- rdrobust(data$y, data$running_var_centered, h = rdd_result$bws[1]*2)
cat("Half bandwidth coefficient:", round(bw_half$coef[1], 4), "\n")
cat("Double bandwidth coefficient:", round(bw_double$coef[1], 4), "\n")

# 2. Different polynomial orders
cat("\n=== ROBUSTNESS: QUADRATIC SPECIFICATION ===\n")
rdd_quad <- rdrobust(data$y, data$running_var_centered, p = 2)
cat("Quadratic specification coefficient:", round(rdd_quad$coef[1], 4), "\n")

# 3. Density test for manipulation
cat("\n=== MANIPULATION TEST ===\n")
density_test <- rddensity(data$running_var_centered)
cat("Density test p-value:", round(density_test$test$p_jk, 4), "\n")

# 4. Placebo test at false cutoff
cat("\n=== PLACEBO TEST ===\n")
false_cutoff <- cutoff + 0.1
data$running_var_placebo <- data$running_var - false_cutoff
placebo_result <- rdrobust(data$y, data$running_var_placebo, c = 0)
cat("Placebo coefficient:", round(placebo_result$coef[1], 4), "\n")
cat("Placebo p-value:", round(placebo_result$pv[1], 4), "\n")

# Summary statistics
cat("\n=== SUMMARY STATISTICS ===\n")
cat("Mean outcome below cutoff:", round(mean(data$y[data$running_var_centered < 0]), 4), "\n")
cat("Mean outcome above cutoff:", round(mean(data$y[data$running_var_centered >= 0]), 4), "\n")
cat("Total observations:", nrow(data), "\n")
```

## 3. Expected Findings
I expect a positive coefficient, indicating that being classified as very-low-birth-weight increases log neonatal mortality. The magnitude should be economically significant (perhaps 0.1-0.5 increase in log mortality), reflecting the serious health implications of this classification. This positive effect could arise through multiple channels: (1) very-low-birth-weight infants genuinely have higher mortality risk due to underdeveloped organs and systems, (2) the classification may trigger different medical protocols or resource allocation, or (3) parental stress and behavioral responses to the classification. The effect should be precisely estimated given the RDD design's local randomization around the threshold.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Exploit the discontinuity at the birth weight threshold for classification.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Crossing the threshold for very-low-birth-weight classification increases neonatal mortality.
